correctness.rationale: For an arbitrary positive period-six word, the six inverse recurrence matrices yield an exact trace=1+determinant polynomial condition. Reduction modulo five yields exactly 13 of 63 nontrivial exponent supports, two rotational orbits of size six plus the all-positive support. The latter is impossible by the strict \(6/5^5+9/5^4+2/5^3<1\) product bound. On each remaining pattern, the three-variable relation decreases strictly in all variables for \(A,B,C\ge5\) and vanishes only at \((5,5,5)\), ruling out unbounded higher division exponents. The two six-equation linear systems have rational rank five and integral primitive solutions \((1,1,2,3,1,4)\) and \((7,2,9,11,4,3)\); all scalars must be positive and coprime to five. Exact substitution establishes sufficiency. Mod-two Fibonacci period three precludes remaining shorter lengths. VERIFY.py independently checks the symbolic polynomial identity, exhaustive 64-word table, both ranks, and exact recurrences. No finite check is claimed to prove the unbounded exponent restriction by itself.

originality.rationale: The original source explicitly displays the two primitive six-cycles and observes that no more were found, but does not prove that no third period-six primitive cycle is possible at arbitrarily large entries. OEIS A214684 enumerates just the first seed. The new assertion is exhaustive all-size uniqueness, plus exclusion of every higher five-division exponent in period-six words; it is stronger than observing examples, primitive gcd normalization, or parity restrictions. published-finding corpus and literature queries located no matching or dominating theorem. Residual uncertainty is unlocated later work, not a claim that search proves global novelty.
residual_risks: A later exhaustive six-cycle classification may exist under a different term or in unindexed literature; negative search findings are not uniqueness proofs.
No independent mathematical validation has yet been performed.

value.rationale: Avila–Khovanova identify five-free dynamics as qualitatively different from both three-free and four-free cases, exhibiting two primitive six-cycles without exhaustive proof. Six is the first possible positive period (periods have to be divisible by three, and three-cycles are excluded). The natural first-cycle stratum is now completely classified, even for arbitrarily large integer initial values, and all higher-power-of-five divisions on six-cycles are ruled out. This replaces experimental examples by a complete structural invariant without suggesting the substantially broader and unproved fate of longer cycles.
